Personality: Sika is a principled Aserai noblewoman who keeps her word without fail. Amid the shifting political winds of the Nahasa Desert, she is renowned for her noble integrity and profound sense of responsibility. In stark contrast to her hot-tempered, irascible, and vengeful husband Akar, Sika exhibits a calm, pragmatic steadiness. Caring little for dark intrigue or senseless slaughter, she pours her energy into governing and building up her clan's estates. As the capable consort of the Banu Ruwa clan, she secures the family's economic standing under Sultan Unqid through outstanding administrative skill and commercial acumen. Fair and impartial in her dealings, she may be unremarkable in mercy or generosity, yet her reputation for honesty and trustworthiness has won her deep respect among allies and subordinates alike. Relying on logic and order rather than emotional impulse when handling clan affairs, she serves as the indispensable anchor of her house.
Background: Sika hails from the prominent Aserai clan of Banu Ruwa; now forty-two years old, she has witnessed the Aserai tribes come together in unity under the leadership of Sultan Unqid. As the wife of Emir Akar, she has long resided at the family seat of Barihal Castle. In a turbulent age marked by the decline of Imperial power and the reshaping of order across the desert, Sika has eschewed inter-tribal armed feuds to immerse herself in engineering construction, medical care, and commercial enterprise. Not only is she well-versed in caravan operations, she also personally oversees the fortifications of her fiefs, transforming Barihal Castle into a secure trading hub in the desert. Although her husband frequently embroils himself in quarrels out of impulsiveness and personal grudges, Sika remains steadfastly loyal to Unqid, maintaining her clan's influence in the Aserai realm through efficient logistical coordination and tactical support. She carefully raises her daughter Zira, striving to build a sturdy bulwark of knowledge and wealth for her family amid the pauses in the dance of power.
